title: What is Microsoft 365 (M365)? Plans, Apps & Price in India 2026
excerpt: Microsoft 365 explained for Indian businesses: how it differs from Office, what Basic, Standard and Premium include, and how GST and licensing work.
body:
Microsoft 365 (M365) is Microsoft's subscription bundle of Office apps (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook), business email, Teams, OneDrive and SharePoint, paid per user per year. For most Indian businesses with fewer than 300 people, the choice comes down to three Business plans: Basic, Standard and Premium. This guide explains what each one includes, how licensing and GST work, and how to pick.

## What is Microsoft 365, and how is it different from Office?

"Office" is the set of applications: Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook. "Microsoft 365" is a subscription that wraps those applications together with cloud services. When you buy a Business plan you are not just buying software to install. You are renting a working environment that includes:

- Business email on your own domain (name@yourcompany.in) through Exchange Online
- Microsoft Teams for chat, calls and meetings
- OneDrive for personal cloud storage and SharePoint for shared team sites
- Web and mobile versions of the Office apps, and on most plans the installed desktop apps too
- Admin tools to create users, reset passwords and assign licences

The older model was a perpetual Office licence: pay once, install on a PC, get no new features, and arrange your own email hosting and file sharing. That model still exists for specific situations such as isolated machines, and we cover it in [Office LTSC 2024 vs Microsoft 365](/blog/microsoft-office-ltsc-2024-vs-microsoft-365). For ordinary office staff, the subscription is usually the better fit because email, storage and meetings come with it. Each user is also licensed to install the desktop apps on several devices rather than one fixed PC, which suits people who move between office, home and phone.

## The Business plans at a glance

Microsoft 365 has two main families. The **Business** plans are priced for small and mid-sized organisations and are capped at 300 users. The **Enterprise** plans have no cap and add compliance tooling. Most Indian SMEs live in the Business family.

| | Business Basic | Business Standard | Business Premium |
|---|---|---|---|
| Installed desktop Office apps | No (web and mobile only) | Yes, on up to five PCs or Macs per user | Yes, same as Standard |
| Business email on your domain | 50 GB mailbox | 50 GB mailbox | 50 GB mailbox |
| Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive | Yes, 1 TB OneDrive | Yes, 1 TB OneDrive | Yes, 1 TB OneDrive |
| Device management (Intune) | No | No | Yes |
| Email threat protection (Defender for Office 365 Plan 1) | No | No | Yes |
| Conditional access (Entra ID Premium P1) | No | No | Yes |
| Document labelling and encryption | No | No | Yes |
| Price per user per year, excl. GST | {{price:microsoft-365-business-basic}} | {{price:microsoft-365-business-standard}} | {{price:microsoft-365-business-premium}} |
| Price per user per year, incl. 18% GST | {{gst:microsoft-365-business-basic}} | {{gst:microsoft-365-business-standard}} | {{gst:microsoft-365-business-premium}} |

All three are sold here on an annual commitment, billed yearly. Prices shown on the website are tentative and exclude GST unless stated; a written quotation fixes the price.

## Business Basic: hosted services without desktop apps

[Microsoft 365 Business Basic](/products/microsoft-365-business-basic) gives each user business email, Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint and the web and mobile versions of the Office apps. What it does not give is installed Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook on a PC.

That is fine for a surprising number of roles. Showroom staff, field engineers, warehouse supervisors and front-desk teams often only need email, Teams and the occasional document in a browser. It is also a sensible choice if you already own desktop Office licences and just need hosted email and collaboration.

The limit is felt by anyone who lives in Excel. Large workbooks, heavy pivot tables and add-ins behave better in the installed application. Before you put a finance team on Basic, ask them to try the web version for a week.

## Business Standard: the usual default

[Microsoft 365 Business Standard](/products/microsoft-365-business-standard) adds the installed desktop applications to everything in Basic. Each user can install Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook on up to five PCs or Macs, plus tablets and phones, and use them with a 50 GB business mailbox, 1 TB of OneDrive and full Teams meetings.

This is the plan most small and mid-sized organisations settle on: accounts teams, CA firms, architects' offices, schools' administrative staff, sales teams. If you are unsure, Standard is the safe starting point, and you can mix it with Basic for people who do not need desktop apps.

## Business Premium: Standard plus security and device control

[Microsoft 365 Business Premium](/products/microsoft-365-business-premium) is Standard with a security and management layer. The applications are the same. The additions are about control:

- **Intune** for enrolling laptops and phones, enforcing a PIN, pushing settings and remotely wiping company data
- **Defender for Office 365 Plan 1** for safe attachments and safe links
- **Entra ID Premium P1** for conditional access (allowing or blocking sign-ins by device, location and risk) and self-service password reset
- **Azure Information Protection** for labelling and encrypting documents
- Windows 11 Business upgrade rights, where the device already has a qualifying Windows Pro licence

The deciding question is usually simple: do staff read work email on personal phones, or do you hold client data under a confidentiality obligation? If yes, Premium is close to necessary. We compare the two in detail in [Business Standard vs Business Premium](/blog/microsoft-365-business-standard-vs-business-premium).

One practical caution: Premium is a capability, not a product that works on arrival. Someone has to configure Intune and conditional access properly, or you risk locking out your own staff.

## The 300-seat cap

The three Business plans are limited to 300 seats in total per tenant, counted across Basic, Standard and Premium together. There is no seat minimum. If you expect to grow past 300, look at the Enterprise plans such as [Microsoft 365 E3](/products/microsoft-365-e3) early. Moving before you hit the ceiling is easier than moving at a renewal deadline, and many organisations start planning at around 250 users.

## Where Copilot fits

Microsoft Copilot is the AI assistant built into the Office apps and Teams. It is not a separate plan in the Business family; it is an add-on that sits on top of a qualifying base licence and is assigned to a named user. On our site you will see it as bundled variants: [Business Standard with Copilot](/products/microsoft-365-business-standard-with-copilot) and [Business Premium with Copilot](/products/microsoft-365-business-premium-with-copilot).

Do not buy it for everyone on day one. Copilot answers using content the signed-in user can already reach, so loose SharePoint permissions become visible quickly. Clean up sharing first, start with a small pilot group, and read [Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing in India](/blog/microsoft-365-copilot-licensing-in-india) before committing.

## What is not included

Quotes go wrong most often over items assumed to be inside the plan. These are generally licensed separately:

- Project and Visio
- Power BI Pro, Dynamics 365 and Azure services
- Extra OneDrive or SharePoint storage beyond the plan allowance
- Audio conferencing and calling plans (Teams includes meetings, but dialling a phone number is an add-on)
- A Windows licence itself (Premium gives upgrade rights, not a licence for a bare machine)

## How licensing works

Microsoft 365 is licensed per user, not per device. You buy seats, and the admin assigns each seat to a named person. When someone leaves, you reassign the licence to their replacement. You can add seats during the term; reductions normally take effect at the annual renewal date, so avoid over-committing in an optimistic quarter.

Mixing plans is allowed and often smart. A twenty-person firm might put the two partners who travel and handle client files on Premium, the accounts team on Standard and the reception and field staff on Basic. Licences are assigned per user, so the spend can follow the risk instead of being uniform.

We supply Microsoft 365 through the Cloud Solution Provider route. If you are choosing between that and a direct agreement, see [CSP vs Enterprise Agreement](/blog/csp-vs-enterprise-agreement-which-microsoft-licensing-model) and our guide on [how to buy genuine Microsoft licences in India](/blog/how-to-buy-genuine-microsoft-licences-in-india).

## GST and invoicing in India

GST at 18% applies to software subscriptions. Prices on this site exclude GST; the {{gst:microsoft-365-business-standard}} figure above for Standard, for example, is the same annual per-user price with 18% added. Every order gets a GST invoice, and a registered business can usually claim the tax as input credit.

Two things protect that credit. First, decide which legal entity will hold the subscription and give us the correct name and GSTIN before the tenant is set up. Second, avoid moving a subscription between entities later; it is an administrative exercise nobody enjoys. Our note on [GST input credit on software purchases](/blog/gst-input-credit-on-software-purchases) walks through the details.

## Common mistakes Indian buyers make

**Buying one plan for everyone.** It is simpler to administer, but it usually overspends on staff who only need email and Teams, and under-protects the few who handle sensitive files. Licence by role.

**Assuming Basic has desktop apps.** The name sounds like a smaller bundle of the same thing. It is not: Basic has no installed Word, Excel, PowerPoint or Outlook. Check this before rollout, because discovering it on day one is awkward.

**Ignoring the admin burden of Premium.** Device management and conditional access need someone to own them. If you have no in-house IT person, ask your IT partner or our team how the setup will be handled.

**Leaving ex-employees licensed.** A seat assigned to someone who left still costs money for the rest of the term. Reassign it to a new joiner, and remember that seat reductions generally only take effect at renewal. Our piece on the [hidden cost of unused software licences](/blog/hidden-cost-of-unused-software-licences) shows how to find them.

**Mixing up the tenant and the invoice.** The company that owns the tenant, the entity named on the invoice and the GSTIN should all agree. Fix this before purchase.

## How to choose: a simple process

1. Count people by role: desk workers, frontline staff, shared-device users.
2. Decide who needs installed apps. In most organisations a quarter to a half do not, and Basic covers them.
3. Decide who needs Premium's controls, person by person rather than as a blanket.
4. Price add-ons such as Copilot separately and pilot them.
5. Confirm the invoicing entity and GSTIN before provisioning.
6. Ask for a written quotation, since a quotation fixes the price.

For a wider comparison with other suites, read [Microsoft 365 vs Google Workspace for Indian SMEs](/blog/microsoft-365-versus-google-workspace-for-indian-smes) and the full [Microsoft 365 licensing guide for Indian businesses](/blog/microsoft-365-licensing-guide-for-indian-businesses). You can see all plans on our [Microsoft 365 page](/microsoft-365), or [request a quotation](/enquiry) and tell us your headcount by role. Monthly and multi-year terms can be quoted on request.

faqs.question: Is Microsoft 365 the same as Microsoft Office?
faqs.answer: No. Office is the set of applications such as Word, Excel and PowerPoint. Microsoft 365 is a subscription that includes those apps (on most plans) plus business email, Teams, OneDrive and SharePoint. A perpetual Office licence has none of the cloud services and does not receive new features.

faqs.question: Which Microsoft 365 Business plan should a small Indian company choose?
faqs.answer: Most small firms start with Business Standard because it includes installed desktop Office apps, a business mailbox, Teams and 1 TB of OneDrive. Choose Basic for staff who only need web and mobile apps, and Premium where personal phones read work mail or client data needs stronger protection.

faqs.question: What is the maximum number of users on Microsoft 365 Business plans?
faqs.answer: The Business plans are capped at 300 seats per tenant, counted across Basic, Standard and Premium combined. There is no minimum seat count. Organisations expecting to pass that ceiling should look at the Enterprise plans early and plan the move before reaching the limit.

faqs.question: Does Microsoft 365 pricing include GST?
faqs.answer: Prices on our website exclude GST, which is 18% on software. Where a page uses the GST-inclusive figure it says so. Each order gets a GST invoice, and a GST-registered business can generally claim the tax as input credit if the invoice carries the correct entity name and GSTIN.

faqs.question: Is Copilot included in Microsoft 365 Business plans?
faqs.answer: No. Copilot is an add-on that sits on top of a qualifying Business plan and is assigned to a named user. We list Standard and Premium bundles with Copilot. Review SharePoint permissions and pilot with a small group before rolling it out widely.

faqs.question: Can I mix Basic, Standard and Premium in one organisation?
faqs.answer: Yes. Licences are assigned per user, so you can put frontline staff on Basic, office staff on Standard and the people who handle sensitive data on Premium. The combined seat count across all three must stay within the 300-seat limit.
